Carlos (Customer): Hey, seeing very high latency on /v1/generate and one 502. Request id 0a1b2c3d4e5f, happened ~2026-03-17T14:05:20Z. Prod, model=text-large, region=us-west-2. Can you pull server-side logs?

Maria (Support): thanks — can you paste the exact request_id and the curl you used? also confirm org_id and whether this is on dedicated or hosted.

Carlos (Customer): request_id is 0a1b2c3d4e5f, org_id=acme-inc. Hosted (API key). Quick curl was similar to below:
```
curl https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"text-large","input":"hello","max_tokens":256}'
```

Ben (Eng): got it. I'll try to locate with that request_id. Typical kibana/ES search we use: index=redwood-prod-requests-* and query: `request_id:\"0a1b2c3d4e5f\" OR trace_id:\"0a1b2c3d4e5f\"` — that should return the API ingress record + router hops.

Ben (Eng): if nothing shows up, logs may have been rolled to cold/archival. Jenna, can you confirm retention for prod requests index?

Jenna (SRE): hot logs kept ~14d, cold tier ~60d, and archives are stored ~90d. If this hit archive, we need a debug bundle or open an archive retrieval.

Jenna (SRE): also check for truncated request_id (sometimes front proxy trims). Try searching for the last 8 chars: `request_id:*2c3d4e5f` and `client_request_id` fields.

Maria (Support): Carlos — would you be comfortable generating a debug bundle? It will include request traces and headers but we will redact API keys. Steps: run the minimal repro curl once, then paste the exact timestamp and we trigger bundle collection.

Maria (Support): Example debug reproduction command to include in bundle (please replace with your real token before running then redact):
```
# reproduce once, capture request id
curl https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"text-large","input":"latency repro","max_tokens":64}'
```

Carlos (Customer): ok doing it now. will send the new request id and exact timestamp in this thread. thanks. :pray:

log-bot: Debug bundle request received. Bundle id db-20260317-77f9. If logs are archived, retrieval ETA ~1-2 hours. S3 path: s3://redwood-archives/debug/db-20260317-77f9 (internal).

Ben (Eng): thanks — once bundle lands I'll run ES query and paste the exact shard docs. If we find a router-level 502 we'll attach the sample traces.

Maria (Support): noted — if archive retrieval is needed we'll update customer on ETA and next steps for root cause.

Carlos (Customer): new attempt done, new request id 1f2e3d4c5b6a at 2026-03-17T14:12:08Z. Upload the bundle as you see fit.

Jenna (SRE): started archive retrieval for original id 0a1b2c3d4e5f (ticket #INC-8892). Will post logs here when available.

Ben (Eng): quick pointer to search query I run in Kibana Discover (paste as one-liner):
```
index: redwood-prod-requests-*
q: request_id:\"0a1b2c3d4e5f\" OR trace_id:\"0a1b2c3d4e5f\" OR client_request_id:\"0a1b2c3d4e5f\"
sort: @timestamp desc
```

Maria (Support): thanks everyone — following up with Carlos once we have logs or archive results. :eyes:
